gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: The film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: After a comma, 'that' is impossible: use 'which'.

gaps.sentence: She has three daughters, all of ___ are at university.
gaps.explanation: 'All of whom' refers to people after 'of'; 'all of which' is for things and 'all of them' cannot join the clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: Everything ___ he said turned out to be true.
The theatre ___ we saw the premiere has been restored beautifully.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' relates to a place: the theatre where we saw…

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.
'What happened next' means 'the thing that happened'; 'that' cannot introduce the clause here because the sentence needs a subject inside it.

gaps.sentence: The shower suddenly stopped working, ___ meant we had to call a plumber.
gaps.hint: refers back to the whole event
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause after a comma.
